summary.headline: IKIO Q4 FY26 revenue rose 47% YoY to INR165 crores and FY26 revenue reached INR595 crores (+23%), with management guiding FY27 revenue growth of 20-22%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 47% YoY and 14% QoQ to INR165 crores, with EBITDA of INR26 crores (margin about 16%) and PAT of INR18 crores (margin about 11%). For FY26, revenue was INR595 crores (+23%), EBITDA INR78 crores (margin about 13%) and PAT INR42 crores (margin about 7%). Non-lighting ("other business") rose to 71% of revenue in FY26 from 57% in FY25, and overseas revenue grew 53% to INR110 crores. Management said front-loaded strategic expenses are keeping margins elevated and that Home Lighting ODM sales to Signify are declining, while working capital has been hit by geopolitical disruption.

up 38% QoQ; vs INR5 crores in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Non-lighting (other business)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR127 crores in Q4 FY26 (+72% YoY) and INR426 crores in FY26 (+53%), now 71% of FY26 revenue. Management estimates non-lighting at about 25% of revenue and expects 25% to rise to 30-32% next year; products include EMS, automotive fuel sensors, solar inverters and batteries, Honeywell products, and Hearables/Wearables.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Management put lighting at about 75% of revenue, with ODM Home Lighting (Signify-linked) about 23% in Q4 per analyst; Home Lighting sales declined YoY. Single-customer share of Home Lighting revenue fell from about 70% and then 50% three years ago.

segments.name: Hearables and Wearables
segments.commentary: About 60% of products are OEM at low margins; EBITDA margin in the high single digits, with a target of double digits. The segment moves to the parent company from Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Middle East / overseas
segments.commentary: Middle East revenue reached about INR43 crores in its first year, per management. Overseas revenue reached INR110 crores in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 20-22% YoY, which management says is cautious given US slowdown.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to be in line with FY26 (about 15-16%); management said gross margin will stay near current levels.
Long-term EBITDA margin target of 18-20%, with a near-term path to 13-14% and then roughly 15%.
FY27 capex of about INR35-36 crores from IPO proceeds, per RHP; management cites 4.5-5x asset turns and about INR1,500 crores top line at full utilisation of about INR300 crores total investment.
Working capital pressure expected to persist for at least 2-3 quarters before normalising.
capex_capacity: Greenfield expansion of about 5 lakh sq ft funded by IPO proceeds: Block I (2 lakh sq ft) commercialised in May 2024; Block II (similar size) expected by end of Q1 FY27.
Headcount about 2,500+ across five factories, up from about 1,600 at IPO.
Management declined to disclose consolidated utilisation; mature units run at about 70%+ and newer lines run lower.
R&D headcount about 80, up from about 40 three years ago.
demand_pricing: Working with all major Indian lighting brands as ODM partner; in auto aftermarket, supplying LED source lamps to multinational brands (started about a couple of months ago, after about a year of development).

Management said it holds about 23-24% of the functional decorative Home Lighting segment (per Frost & Sullivan, as of 2023), and claims to be among the largest in commercial and refrigeration lighting.
Pricing is mostly BOM-plus with a 2-3 month lag to pass through raw material and FX moves; in-store lighting is priced on market and solution.
Rising metal prices and longer component lead times are affecting supply chain and working capital; the company says it is passing through costs.
Management says it is slow in the US because of tariffs and geopolitics; Middle East disruption has also affected supply chain and orders.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated headcount and utilisation level?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount is 2,500+ across all factories versus about 1,600 at IPO. Mature units run at about 70%+ utilisation; newer verticals run lower and should improve with volumes. Management declined to give a consolidated figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an order book?
qa_highlights.answer: No order book; revenue visibility comes from customer planning forecasts. The ODM model means each new category is screened for feasibility, EBITDA margin and value addition before entry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall after the IPO, and will they recover to 20-22%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall to onboarding fixed costs for new verticals (Automotive Lighting, Hearables, Honeywell, EMS, Energy). Margins have risen for 4-5 quarters; the target is 18-20%, with about 15% reached so far.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 CapEx and full-utilisation revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR35-36 crores of capex this year from IPO proceeds. On roughly INR300 crores of total investment at 4.5-5x asset turns, management pointed to about INR1,500 crores top line at full utilisation, as an intent rather than a timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and comparison with EMS peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is elevated because of inventory built during geopolitical disruption and design changes; the company expects 2-3 quarters before normalising. Management said it owns designs and buys raw materials, which explains the gap with EMS peers that run negative working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly BOM-plus with a 2-3 month lag, except in-store lighting, which is market-priced. No annual price-reduction contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Is Gravus Tech a move into B2C?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the Gravus acquisition (88% stake) is for B2B high-end project and export business, serving architects and designers.

risks_watch: Declining ODM Home Lighting sales to Signify (and its JV entity) and dependence on a few customers.
US expansion has slowed; management expects results only in 2-3 quarters.
Working capital stretch and inventory build; payable and receivable days were not disclosed.
Margins depend on new verticals reaching volume; Hearables OEM mix and new automotive lines are still sub-scale.
Middle East war and supply-chain disruption; rising aluminium and copper prices and longer component lead times.
Block II commissioning by end of Q1 FY27 and Hearables shift to the parent company.
Management did not give R&D spend figures and said it would disclose them next time. Utilisation disclosure is still lacking.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and diversification, with the Middle East and new verticals highlighted. Cautious and somewhat evasive on the US market, working capital, utilisation and R&D spend, and it deferred several numbers to future calls or a site visit.
key_quotes: So we don't have an order book kind of situation with our customers.
And we believe that this trend will continue, although now that we've reached a level of around 15%.

So if I talk of the CapEx first, then we are, I think, left with around -- from the IPO proceeds, somewhere around INR35 crores, INR36 crores of CapEx, which we intend to utilize in this financial year.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 20-22% (called cautious given US slowdown), backed partly by Block II of the 5 lakh sq ft greenfield expansion due by end Q1 FY27 and INR35-36 crore IPO-funded capex, plus new products (auto LED source lamps) and Middle East growth, but no disclosed order book and the US business has not started.
